## Milestone 1 - Task 4.1/4.2/4.3: Decision Orchestrator

Consumes the Normalized Response Contract produced by 04-response-normalizer (docs/contracts/normalized-response-contract.md) and produces a Decision Contract (docs/contracts/decision-contract.md) via a three-tier funnel (docs/architecture/decision-agent-design.md section 1):

- Tier 0: transport.status_code === null -> BLOCKED, no AI.
- Tier 1: expected.status exists and exactly equals the actual status code -> PASS, no AI.
- Tier 2: everything else -> build an evidence packet, call Claude once, validate its structured response.

Task 4.2 extracted Tier 0 + Tier 1 + final contract assembly into the 'Decision Engine' node group (see that sticky). Task 4.3 extracted the AI path's prompt construction into a dedicated 'Prompt Builder' stage, separate from the Anthropic API-call assembly (see the AI Evaluation Note sticky). Tier routing and the Decision Contract's shape are unchanged since Task 4.1.

This workflow still does not implement confidence recalibration, grounding validation, retry logic, or AI-failure recovery (later tasks), and never implements Documentation Agent or Jira Agent.

## Security notes

- The Claude node's URL is a fixed literal (https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages), never built from item data - no SSRF surface here (unlike the HTTP Executor, which sends to a test-provided URL by design).
- The API key is never read from item data or $env in this workflow - it's supplied via an n8n Header Auth credential (see 'Claude' node), so it never appears in workflow JSON or execution data. See n8n/credentials.example.json.
- response_body in the evidence packet is capped (Build Evidence Packet) so an oversized or adversarial target-API response can't blow up AI cost or request size.
- tool_choice forces the model to call return_verdict with a fixed JSON Schema - it cannot return free-form text, which bounds a prompt-injection attempt from an adversarial response body to 'pick a wrong enum/string within this schema', not arbitrary output or tool access. This narrows, but does not eliminate, injection risk - full grounding/hallucination defenses are Task 4.4, not this workflow.

## Task 4.1 design notes

- 'Route Validation Errors' mirrors the same-named pattern in 03-http-executor.json: an item that's already an ERROR payload (upstream, or from 'Validate Contract') skips the Decision Engine and AI entirely.
- Decision Engine Tier 0 and Tier 1 each check '__verdict' from the previous tier before doing their own check, so at most one tier ever resolves a given item.
- The 0.7 confidence threshold gating PASS/FAIL vs MANUAL_REVIEW in 'Validate Decision Contract' is docs/contracts/decision-contract.md's own already-published Verdict States rule, enforced here as contract validation - the confidence VALUE itself is never adjusted (that's confidence recalibration, explicitly out of scope for this task).
- AI_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (Claude node's error output) is deliberately a single generic code, not a classifier like 03's - anything more is 'AI failure recovery', out of scope here.

## Decision Engine (Task 4.2)

The three nodes below - 'Decision Engine - Tier 0 (Transport)', 'Decision Engine - Tier 1 (Exact Match)', 'Decision Engine - Finalize' - are the dedicated, reusable component that generates a complete Decision Contract for every case that doesn't need AI. AI invocation stays isolated to Tier 2 (right side of this workflow) - nothing in this group ever calls Claude.

Evidence is built as structured objects internally (e.g. `{ type: 'status_code', expected: 200, actual: 200 }`) and only rendered to the array-of-strings shape docs/contracts/decision-contract.md requires in 'Decision Engine - Finalize' - the contract itself is unchanged, only this group's internal representation is (Task 4.2).

Kept as an in-workflow node group rather than extracted to a separate sub-workflow file: this project has never yet exercised a real n8n cross-workflow Execute Workflow call (every 'hand-off' NoOp so far is conceptual, not wired), and introducing that unverified mechanism here would add risk beyond this task's scope. The group's minimal external coupling (works only off __-prefixed fields it owns) makes it a low-effort lift into a sub-workflow later, once live n8n verification is possible.

## AI Evaluation (Task 4.3)

The Tier 2 component: 'Build Evidence Packet' -> 'Prompt Builder' -> 'Build Claude API Request' -> 'Claude' -> 'Validate Decision Contract' (or 'Build AI Service Error' on failure). Only reached when the Decision Engine (left) couldn't resolve a case without AI.

'Prompt Builder' is the dedicated stage this task adds: it re-verifies the evidence packet against the allow-listed keys (defense in depth on top of 'Build Evidence Packet''s own construction) and builds the system prompt + user message text - separately from 'Build Claude API Request', which owns only the Anthropic API-call structure (model, tool schema, tool_choice). Splitting these two means a future model swap or parameter change never risks touching the prompt/evidence-allow-list logic, and vice versa.

'Validate Decision Contract' is unchanged from Task 4.1/4.2 - still no retry, no grounding validation, no confidence recalibration (later tasks).

nodes.notes: Hand-off boundary to the Documentation Agent (and, for next_action: create_jira, the Jira Agent) - both Task 4+, not yet built. Receives either a Decision Contract (docs/contracts/decision-contract.md) or an ERROR payload (docs/contracts/error-payload.md). No Excel write or Jira ticket drafting happens in this workflow.
